purpose: Materialize the currently reproducible public POSS-I transient/data-product evidence as machine-readable rows for later day-level comparison with the EARTH ledger. This version is intentionally cohort/data-product level because the exact 312 observation-day table has not yet been materialized here.

representation_contract.target_invariant: detector-bound POSS-I transient/candidate structure and observation opportunity
must_preserve: which results are preregistered versus post-hoc
whether a row describes a dataset, cohort, model result or detector control
must_not_infer: external astrophysical source identity from a point-like plate detection
UAP identity from a POSS-I candidate
cross-domain event identity without exact dates and independent controls

rows.bridge_blocker: Catalogue rows do not themselves carry the day-level join key in this compact Janus-Cosmos ledger.

rows.exposure_boundary: Processed tile-time denominator, not exact non-overlapping geometric sky area-time.

rows.binary_identity: ANY_CANDIDATE == PALOMAR_OBSERVED_NIGHT in the dense S0 cohort

rows.reported_failure: approximately 11 arcsec astrometry defect on affected tiles allowed ordinary stars to evade catalogue vetoes

rows.interpretation: Candidate density is strongly field-dependent; sky position must be modeled before temporal/contextual interpretation.

rows.important_boundary: A tile absent from stage_S0.csv is not absent from the footprint; observation opportunity must come from the manifest, not from candidate-present rows.

rows.interpretation: An independent digitization of the same POSS-I E plates does not confirm two fifths of this candidate catalogue. This locates a major detector/digitization disagreement but does not by itself identify which representation is physically correct.

rows.required_object: 312-row unique observation-day ledger with candidate count, tile/plate opportunity and frozen nuclear-window annotations
rows.reason: The public upstream candidate and tile tables are shipped as compressed binary data products; their hashes and counts are bound, but this pass has not yet imported the day-level table into Janus-Cosmos.
rows.scientific_effect: Exact EARTH<->SPACE day joins remain BLOCKED rather than silently approximated.

next_actions: Materialize the 312 unique observation dates from public plate/tile metadata and bind their source hashes.
For every observation day, record candidate_count, plate_count, tile_count, exposure opportunity and sky-position summaries.
Join nuclear-test windows only after the observation-day ledger is frozen.
Keep detector/artifact controls as first-class columns rather than post-hoc exclusions.
Only expose day rows to the EARTH bridge after this ledger is source-complete enough to distinguish NO_OBSERVATION from OBSERVED_ZERO.
canonical_seal: THE SPACE LEDGER COUNTS THE DETECTOR AND ITS OPPORTUNITY BEFORE IT COUNTS A TRANSIENT. A POINT ON A PLATE IS NOT YET A SOURCE IN THE WORLD.
